# Eclipse Cooling vs. Albedo Darkening in Europa's Ice Shell

**Separating the sub-Jovian eclipse-cooling contribution to ice-shell thickness from the
trailing-hemisphere albedo (darkening) contribution, and estimating the shell in the
hypothetical absence of any darkening process.**

*Tier 1 analysis — existing PTM3D output only (no new simulations). Generated by
`scripts/eclipse_vs_albedo_analysis.py`; figures in
`plots/ice-shell-dynamics/eclipse_analysis/`.*

---

## 1. Setup

Europa's modeled ice shell carries two distinct **longitude-dependent** thickness signals:

- **`b11^c` (sub-Jovian / anti-Jovian)** — an *insolation* asymmetry. The sub-Jovian
  hemisphere is **eclipsed by Jupiter** once per orbit, producing a localized deficit in
  the annual-mean direct insolation, slightly offset by **Jupiter-shine** (reflected
  sunlight + Jupiter thermal IR).
- **`b11^s` (leading / trailing)** — an *albedo* asymmetry from **trailing-hemisphere
  darkening** (the spatially variable Bond-albedo map).

We isolate these two by comparing two existing 288-timestep ICO6 (81,920-face) runs,
both N–S symmetrized:

| Run | Albedo | Output dir | Role |
|-----|--------|-----------|------|
| **No darkening** | uniform A = 0.5 | `output/europa_ico6_uniform-ice` | eclipse + Jupiter-shine only (no leading/trailing albedo signal) |
| **With darkening** | spatial Bond-albedo map | `output/europa_ico6_albedo-map` | adds the leading/trailing albedo signal |

Surface temperatures feed the Ojakangas & Stevenson (1989) equilibrium shell model
($C_R = 0.85$) for four rheologies. Gridding uses **periodic longitude padding** to
avoid the λ = ±180° seam artifact that plain `griddata` produces.

## 2. Geophysics — no-darkening vs with-darkening (all coefficients in km)

| Case | Run | ⟨b⟩ | $b_{11}^c$ | $b_{11}^s$ | $b_{20}$ | $b_{22}^c$ | $4t_{22}$ | $t_{20}{+}2t_{22}$ | $\Delta(B{-}A)/C$ | $\Delta(B{-}C)/A$ | Stability |
|------|-----|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:|:--:|
| Maxwell $H$=0   | no darkening | 19.59 | **+0.212** | +0.003 | −3.079 | +1.443 | 5.77 | −0.19 | 5.8e−7 | **−1.9e−8** | **STABLE** |
| Maxwell $H$=0   | darkening    | 20.19 | +0.359 | **−1.277** | −2.685 | +1.458 | 5.83 | +0.23 | 5.8e−7 | **+2.3e−8** | unstable |
| Maxwell $H$=10  | no darkening | 15.90 | +0.171 | +0.002 | −1.435 | +0.895 | 3.58 | +0.35 | 3.6e−7 | +3.5e−8 | unstable |
| Maxwell $H$=10  | darkening    | 16.40 | +0.290 | −1.041 | −1.093 | +0.903 | 3.61 | +0.71 | 3.6e−7 | +7.1e−8 | unstable |
| Flow $n_G$=3    | no darkening | 25.16 | +0.267 | +0.004 | −1.358 | +1.180 | 4.72 | +1.00 | 4.7e−7 | +1.0e−7 | unstable |
| Flow $n_G$=3    | darkening    | 25.94 | +0.456 | −1.651 | −0.795 | +1.189 | 4.76 | +1.58 | 4.8e−7 | +1.6e−7 | unstable |
| Flow $n_G$=5.2  | no darkening | 13.40 | +0.142 | +0.002 | −0.409 | +0.558 | 2.23 | +0.71 | 2.2e−7 | +7.1e−8 | unstable |
| Flow $n_G$=5.2  | darkening    | 13.82 | +0.242 | −0.880 | −0.102 | +0.561 | 2.25 | +1.02 | 2.2e−7 | +1.0e−7 | unstable |

**The albedo and eclipse signals are cleanly separated:**
- Without darkening, **`b11^s` ≈ 0** (±0.003 km) — the leading/trailing signal is entirely
  an albedo effect.
- The **`b11^c` (sub-Jovian) signal survives without darkening** (+0.14 to +0.27 km across
  rheologies) — it is an insolation/eclipse effect, independent of the albedo map.
- Darkening leaves `b11^c` and the tidal `b22^c` largely intact but adds the large
  `b11^s` ≈ −0.9 to −1.7 km (leading hemisphere thicker) and raises `b20` (less negative).

*(See **F1** surface-temperature maps, **F3** thickness maps, **F4** harmonic bars.)*

## 3. The sub-Jovian signal is eclipse-driven, not Jupiter-shine

> ⚠️ **STALE — the Jupiter IR row below was computed before PTM-40 (2026-08-03).** The primary
> IR view factor was `Ω/(4π)` where it should have been `Ω/π`, so **every Jupiter IR number in
> this table is exactly 4× too low**. The correction is a pure geometric factor, verified at
> ratio 4.0000, and it does not touch direct solar or Jupiter reflected — so the corrected row
> can be written down exactly without re-running:
>
> | Component | sub-Jovian (0°) | leading (90°) | anti-Jovian (180°) | trailing (270°) |
> |-----------|----:|----:|----:|----:|
> | Jupiter IR **(corrected)** | **0.152** | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.004 |
>
> **Corrected Jupiter-shine total at sub-Jovian: 0.025 + 0.152 = 0.177 W m⁻², so the eclipse
> deficit is ~9.2× larger than Jupiter-shine, not ~26×.** The section's conclusion is unchanged
> and in fact rests on the same sign: Jupiter-shine still *warms* the sub-Jovian hemisphere and
> still only partly offsets a 1.62 W m⁻² eclipse deficit. The 2.3 K sub-Jovian cold anomaly
> shrinks by roughly 0.1 W m⁻² of forcing (≈7 % of the deficit), which does not change any
> qualitative statement in §3–§5.
>
> The table was **not regenerated**: the flux components are simulation outputs, so refreshing
> them means re-running both 288-timestep ICO6 (81,920-face) arms. That is not cheap, and the
> ×4 is exact, so the corrected value is stated inline instead. Any *quantitative* reuse of
> §3 should re-run first. Nothing else in this document is affected — the geophysics in §2 and
> §4 derives from temperature, whose Jupiter-IR sensitivity is the ≈0.1 W m⁻² above.

The uniform-ice run stores each flux component separately. Annual-mean equatorial flux at
the cardinal longitudes (W m⁻²):

| Component | sub-Jovian (0°) | leading (90°) | anti-Jovian (180°) | trailing (270°) |
|-----------|----:|----:|----:|----:|
| Direct solar | **15.11** | 16.68 | 16.78 | 16.72 |
| Jupiter reflected | 0.025 | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.001 |
| Jupiter IR *(stale, ×4 low — see above)* | 0.038 | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.001 |

- **Eclipse deficit:** direct insolation dips to 15.11 W m⁻² at the sub-Jovian meridian
  versus ~16.7 elsewhere — a **localized ~1.62 W m⁻² (≈10%) deficit**. The deficit is
  confined near sub-Jovian (the other three cardinal points are nearly equal), the
  signature of an **eclipse** (a brief shadow at one orbital phase), *not* a smooth
  eccentricity cosine.
- **Jupiter-shine** (reflected + IR) totals only ~~0.062~~ **0.177 W m⁻²** at sub-Jovian
  (corrected for PTM-40) — ~~~26×~~ **~9.2× smaller** than the eclipse deficit — and *warms*
  the sub-Jovian hemisphere, slightly *opposing* the eclipse cooling.

So the sub-Jovian shell thickening (cooler → thicker) is **overwhelmingly an eclipse
effect**; Jupiter reflected sunlight and Jupiter thermal IR are negligible. The
sub-Jovian equator is ~2.3 K colder than the rest of the equator (107.8 K vs ~110 K).

*(See **F2** flux-component maps + equatorial profile — the clean localized dip.)*

## 4. Dynamics in the absence of trailing-hemisphere darkening

- **Maxwell $H$=0 is dynamically STABLE without darkening** ($\Delta(B{-}C)/A = -1.9\times10^{-8}$):
  the eclipse-driven `t20`/`t22` pattern alone keeps $C > B > A$. Trailing-hemisphere
  **darkening flips it to unstable** ($+2.3\times10^{-8}$) — consistent with the main study.
- The other three rheologies are **marginally unstable with or without darkening**;
  darkening increases $\Delta(B{-}C)/A$ by 30–60%.
- $\Delta(B{-}A)/C$ (the equatorial-ellipticity moment, set by tidal $4t_{22}$) is **robust**:
  it changes by <1% between the two runs — confirming the tidal pattern dominates it and
  neither eclipse nor albedo moves it.

**Implication:** in a hypothetical Europa with no trailing-hemisphere darkening, the
eclipse-only insolation asymmetry is *not* destabilizing for the (stiffest) Maxwell $H$=0
shell; the trailing-darkening albedo dichotomy is what tips that case into the
polar-wander-unstable regime. For the softer/flow-law shells the eclipse-only world is
already marginally unstable, and darkening deepens it.

*(See **F5** MoI/stability bars.)*

## 5. First-order `b11^c` attribution (linearized — with caveat)

Linearizing each component's longitude-anomalous flux to a temperature perturbation
$\delta T = \text{absorptivity}\cdot(F-\langle F\rangle_\lambda)/(4\varepsilon\sigma T^3)$
and propagating through the thickness model gives each component's contribution to
`b11^c` (km):

| Case | eclipse | Jupiter refl | Jupiter IR | sum | actual `b11^c` | residual |
|------|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:|
| Maxwell $H$=0  | +0.363 | −0.005 | −0.016 | +0.342 | +0.212 | **−0.129** |
| Maxwell $H$=10 | +0.286 | −0.004 | −0.012 | +0.270 | +0.171 | −0.099 |
| Flow $n_G$=3   | +0.446 | −0.007 | −0.019 | +0.420 | +0.267 | −0.153 |
| Flow $n_G$=5.2 | +0.235 | −0.004 | −0.010 | +0.222 | +0.142 | −0.080 |

The linearized **eclipse term overshoots the actual `b11^c` by ~60%** (large negative
residual). This is the **thermal-inertia / nonlinearity bias**: the eclipse is a *transient*
(a brief shadow at local noon), so the regolith buffers it and the $\langle T^4\rangle \ne
\langle T\rangle^4$ nonlinearity reduces its true annual-mean imprint well below the
linearized time-averaged-flux estimate. The qualitative split (**eclipse ≫ Jupiter-shine,
which is negligible and opposing**) is robust; the **exact eclipse magnitude in temperature
is not reliably recovered at Tier 1** and would require the controlled runs in §7.

*(See **F6** attribution waterfall.)*

| Energy balance @ sub-Jovian equator | absorbed 7.60 W m⁻² → $T_{rad}$=109.0 K vs actual 107.8 K (1.2 K gap from thermal-inertia/$\langle T^4\rangle$) ✓ |

The **ICO6/ICO7 provenance gap is resolved**: the published `b11`/`b22` values (attributed
to ICO7 in the slides) are reproduced by the present ICO6 data to within ~0.01–0.04 km, as
expected since these are degree-1/2 signals that converge far below the mesh resolution.
`scripts/plot_ice_shell.py` default paths were repointed from the now-missing
`output/europa_global_ico7*` to the present ICO6 dirs.

## 7. Limitations & the path to a rigorous eclipse magnitude (Tier 2)

1. **Thermal-inertia bias (central).** The §5 linearized eclipse magnitude overshoots by
   ~60%; only the *direction* (eclipse cools sub-Jovian) and the *eclipse ≫ Jupiter-shine*
   ranking are robust at Tier 1.
2. **Eclipse temporal resolution.** 288 steps/orbit ≈ 18-min cadence may under-resolve
   eclipse ingress/egress; the absolute eclipse depth in the existing run could be mildly
   aliased.
3. **Stability knife-edge.** $\Delta(B{-}C)/A$ flips at the ~10⁻⁸ level. The no-darkening
   run is A=0.5; the darkening model's bright endmember is A=0.55 (~3 K warmer), which
   could shift the Maxwell $H$=0 verdict. The sign reported here uses A=0.5.

**Tier 2 (deferred, recommended if the eclipse magnitude must be pinned):** add an
`enable_primary_eclipse` flag to the PTM3D illumination model (~10 lines, ANDed into the
four `if (!primary_is_sun_)` eclipse guards in
`src/cpp/illumination/illumination_model.cpp`), rebuild, and run 3 ICO6 thermal
experiments at uniform albedo — eclipse-off, reflected-off, both-off — to obtain the
thermally-exact eclipse-vs-Jupiter-shine split. Optionally add a uniform A=0.55 reference
to settle the stability knife-edge.

## 8. PTM3D uniform-albedo vs. O&S analytical thermal model

A direct comparison of the **PTM3D uniform-albedo thermal model** (eclipse + Jupiter
reflected + Jupiter IR, thermal inertia, A = 0.5) against the **O&S analytical surface-
temperature model** (axisymmetric radiative equilibrium, same A = 0.5, no eclipse / no
Jupiter-shine / no thermal inertia). The difference isolates everything the 3-D thermal
physics adds at *fixed albedo*. Produced by `scripts/compare_ptm3d_vs_os.py`.

| Quantity | O&S analytical | PTM3D uniform | PTM3D − O&S |
|----------|---------------:|--------------:|------------:|
| Global-mean $T_s$ | 101.3 K | 102.2 K | +0.9 K |
| Equator (zonal mean) | 108.8 K | 109.3 K | +0.4 K |
| Pole (zonal mean) | 52.1 K | 53.9 K | +1.8 K |
| Sub-Jovian equatorial dip (vs own zonal mean) | 0 (axisymmetric) | −1.5 K | — |
| Full-map $\Delta T_s$ range | — | — | −1.1 … +6.7 K |
| Mean thickness, Maxwell $H$=0 | 19.72 km | 19.56 km | — |
| Thickness $\Delta b$ range (Maxwell $H$=0) | — | — | −1.66 … +0.31 km |

**Three differences emerge (C1, C2):**
1. **The zonal pole-to-equator structure agrees** — the two models nearly overlap in
   zonal-mean $T_s(\theta)$, confirming the PTM3D run and the O&S radiative-equilibrium
   model share the same albedo and insolation budget.
2. **Thermal inertia warms the poles** by ~1–2 K in the zonal mean (up to +6.7 K locally),
   because the 3-D model stores and redistributes heat rather than assuming instantaneous
   radiative equilibrium of the annual-average insolation. This *thins* the polar shell by
   up to ~1.7 km relative to O&S.
3. **The eclipse adds a sub-Jovian dip** (−1.5 K at the equator) that the axisymmetric O&S
   model cannot represent at all; it *thickens* the sub-Jovian shell by ~+0.3 km. This is
   the `b11^c` signal that O&S (with `b11^c` ≡ 0) lacks.

So at fixed albedo the PTM3D−O&S thickness difference is **dominated by polar thinning
(thermal inertia)**, with the **eclipse-driven sub-Jovian thickening** as the leading
*longitude-dependent* (degree-1) departure.
